post.caption: The Met's Cellini cup was a copy. The Metropolitan Museum in New York keeps a gold cup with enamel called the Rospigliosi Cup, after a noble family of Rome. For years it was credited to the Renaissance master Benvenuto Cellini. Collector Benjamin Altman left it to the Met in 1913. Then a conservator took the cup apart and found work from the 1800s. The Met now describes it as a copy. It is linked to Reinhold Vasters, a goldsmith from Aachen, Germany, whose drawings sat unnoticed in a London museum for decades. The Met holds dozens of pieces attributed to him. Vasters died in 1909 at age 82.
